text.arabic_uthmani: أَفَلَا يَتُوبُونَ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَهُۥ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ

words.gloss_range: consequential interrogative opening that bridges the prior warning into rebuking invitation
words.prose: {{ar:أَفَ}} ({{tr:a-fa}}) opens with question force and consequence at once: the warning in 5:73 is not left sealed, but is turned immediately into an appeal. The fused particle stack makes the ayah arrive as a follow-up, while the sharp opening sound helps the rebuke feel like an interruption that asks why return has not followed.

topics.headline: question and consequence fused
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins as a consequence-bearing question, not as a detached new statement.
topics.reason: QAC identifies hamza interrogative plus consequential fa, and the local clause is a rhetorical question after 5:73; the CRITICAL rows preserve that joint force.

topics.headline: warning carried into invitation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees mercy opening from inside the prior warning rather than after a reset.
topics.reason: The boundary rows are compatible with the fa linkage noted in QAC: 5:74 follows 5:73 as appeal after warning.

topics.headline: visible and audible launch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the question force begin before any verb is reached.
topics.reason: The surface form and opening hamza support the CRITICAL claim that interrogative force is audible from the first beat.

words.gloss_range: negation particle whose surface denial is reversed by the rhetorical question into pressure toward action
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) names the absent action while the interrogative frame presses toward the positive: why are they not turning and seeking covering? Its independent particle shape lets the negation govern the coordinated verbal span, so the missing duty is a paired absence rather than only the first verb.

topics.headline: one negator over the paired verbs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wording treats turning and seeking covering as one missing paired response.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence coordinates the two verbs inside one rhetorical question, so the negator's scope over the pair is locally licensed.

topics.headline: negation reversed into invitation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears both the current non-action and the implied demand that it should change.
topics.reason: QAC explicitly treats the hamza plus {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) construction as a rhetorical question expecting positive action.

topics.headline: hinge before the first verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the withheld action suspended just before the verb names it.
topics.reason: The particle sits between the interrogative opening and the first imperfect verb, matching the CRITICAL hinge and sound-delay claims.

words.gloss_range: imperfect Form I human turning, locally intransitive and directed toward God by the following prepositional phrase
words.root_gloss_range: {{ar:ت و ب}} ({{tr:t-w-b}}) centers on return and repentance; local grammar selects human moral reorientation toward a named goal

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: directional goal phrase completing the return verb

words.prose: {{ar:يَتُوبُونَ}} ({{tr:yatūbūna}}) turns the particle pressure into a specific action: present, available reorientation rather than a completed past act or a bare imperative. Its Form I intransitive frame waits for {{ar:إِلَى ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:ilā allāhi}}), so repentance is heard as movement toward a terminus. The plural form keeps the group from 5:73 in view, and its -ūna cadence pairs with the next human-action verb before the ayah shifts into the nominal attribute answer. The same Surah 5 return-thread, including 5:39 and 5:71, makes this polemical moment part of a wider invitation pattern.

topics.headline: presently available return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wording presses a still-open action rather than reporting a closed failure or issuing a plain command.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an imperfect third-person plural verb inside a rhetorical question, supporting the CRITICAL contrast with perfect and imperative alternatives.

topics.headline: return completed by direction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees repentance as re-aimed movement toward God, not only inward remorse.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces {{ar:إِلَى}} ({{tr:ilā}}) plus the divine name as the prepositional complement of this intransitive verb.

topics.headline: same group kept under appeal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the condemned group remain grammatically reachable by an appeal to return.
topics.reason: The 3mp agreement supplies the implicit subject and is consistent with continuity from the prior polemical context.

topics.headline: return image narrowed to repentance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the concrete return image while local grammar selects moral repentance toward God.
topics.reason: The dictionary evidence supports return and repentance branches, but the local imperfect with {{ar:إِلَى ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:ilā allāhi}}) narrows that field to moral reorientation.

topics.headline: Surah 5 return pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes this invitation as part of Surah 5's repeated return logic, including 5:39 and 5:71.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide concrete same-surah references, and no guardrail evidence contradicts the local echo.

topics.headline: paired human-action cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the first human-action verb prepare both the second verb and the later shift into stable divine attributes.
topics.reason: The two imperfect verbs are coordinated in one question before the final nominal sentence, supporting the rhythm and structural transition rows.

words.gloss_range: directional preposition marking God as the endpoint and telos of return

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: divine name governed by the preposition as the return endpoint

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَى}} ({{tr:ilā}}) makes the return destination-forward. It governs {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) and turns the verb into a trajectory: the issue is not only leaving the prior error but moving toward a named endpoint. The human-direction frame also contrasts with divine-acceptance frames that use an upon relation.

topics.headline: destination foregrounded
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that repentance is aimed toward God, not merely away from a mistake.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify {{ar:إِلَى}} ({{tr:ilā}}) as the preposition that supplies the goal of {{ar:يَتُوبُونَ}} ({{tr:yatūbūna}}).

topics.headline: preposition binds the divine name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the preposition and divine name functioning as one goal phrase.
topics.reason: The genitive governance of the following divine name is syntactically forced.

topics.headline: human turning toward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the agency difference: humans turn toward, while divine acceptance is framed differently elsewhere.
topics.reason: The local human verb takes {{ar:إِلَى}} ({{tr:ilā}}), and the CRITICAL rows validly contrast this with other tawba frames without changing the local parse.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name in genitive goal position after the directional preposition
words.root_gloss_range: {{ar:أ ل ه}} ({{tr:ʾ-l-h}}) includes worship and disputed bewilderment derivations; locally the fixed proper name selects the named divine referent as return-goal

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition governing the first divine-name occurrence
second divine-name occurrence as nominative answer subject

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) is the named endpoint of return, not a generic deity term. Its genitive case is governed by {{ar:إِلَى}} ({{tr:ilā}}), and that first role prepares the later nominative {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:allāhu}}): the same name is first the goal of human movement and then the subject who answers with attributes. After the disputed claim in 5:73, the name is repaired by being made the direction of correction. The derivational field can add worship and bewilderment pressure, but the local surface keeps the fixed proper name and the goal role primary.

topics.headline: named endpoint of return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees repentance directed to the named God, not to an abstract moral direction.
topics.reason: The word is a proper divine name governed by the preceding preposition as the goal of return.

topics.headline: genitive goal before nominative subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated divine name changing grammatical role inside the ayah.
topics.reason: QAC and noun-instance evidence distinguish the genitive word 5 occurrence from the nominative word 9 occurrence.

topics.headline: worship and bewilderment field narrowed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the return as re-centering worship and confusion while still reading the fixed proper name as the local sense.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute is valid as pressure, but local grammar and form select the proper divine name rather than a common-noun or distraction sense.

topics.headline: name repairs the prior claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the divine name moved from the prior disputed claim into the direction of correction.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows tie the local role to 5:73 and to the ayah's return-covering-mercy sequence without contradicting the syntactic role.

topics.headline: first anchor of the name repetition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the ayah around two occurrences of the same name: goal first, answer subject later.
topics.reason: The local repetition of the divine name is structurally meaningful because the two occurrences occupy different roles.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction binding the second imperfect verb to the first inside the same rhetorical question
words.prose: The first {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps seeking covering inside the same question as turning. It joins the two imperfect verbs as co-present responses rather than alternatives or separate clauses, and its fused surface before the long second verb makes the paired obligation visible and audible.

topics.headline: two verbs under one question
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that turning and seeking covering are joined as one response frame.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence explicitly coordinates the second verb with {{ar:يَتُوبُونَ}} ({{tr:yatūbūna}}) in the rhetorical question.

topics.headline: not an optional appendix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second action as a necessary partner rather than a loose afterthought.
topics.reason: The conjunction's local position between the two imperfect verbs supports equal coordination without sequence being specified.

topics.headline: short connector fused to second verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the second action enter as attached continuation, not a fresh launch.
topics.reason: The surface conjunction is proclitic to the following verb in recitation and spelling behavior, matching the CRITICAL sound-form rows.

words.gloss_range: imperfect Form X requestive verb: seeking God's protective covering/forgiveness, with the divine object compressed in the suffix
words.root_gloss_range: {{ar:غ ف ر}} ({{tr:gh-f-r}}) ranges from covering and concealment to forgiveness; local Form X selects seeking that covering from God

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: same-root intensive predicate answering the requestive verb

words.prose: {{ar:يَسْتَغْفِرُونَهُۥ}} ({{tr:yastaghfirūnahū}}) completes the paired human response as ongoing seeking, not human covering. Form X makes them request the {{ar:غ ف ر}} ({{tr:gh-f-r}}) quality, while the attached suffix makes many plural seekers converge on one divine object. The root image of protective covering remains useful, but it is locally narrowed into a plea for divine forgiveness and shielding; after 5:73's exposure and threat, that covering becomes remedy rather than concealment of truth. The same root then returns as {{ar:غَفُورٌ}} ({{tr:ghafūrun}}), so the request already points to the answer and to Surah 5's covering-mercy closures at 5:3, 5:34, 5:39, and 5:98.

topics.headline: ongoing request, not human covering
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the subjects are seekers of covering, not the agents who provide it.
topics.reason: QAC identifies Form X as requestive and the attachment evidence places the verb inside the same rhetorical question as the first imperfect.

topics.headline: plural seekers face one divine object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the request as personally directed to God, not abstract forgiveness-seeking.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence syntactically forces the clitic suffix as the direct object and QAC links it back to the divine name.

topics.headline: protective covering as forgiveness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the shielding image behind forgiveness while the local Form X frame keeps the sense as seeking divine pardon and protection.
topics.reason: The dictionary supports covering and forgiveness branches, but local requestive grammar selects seeking forgiveness/protective covering from God rather than unrelated branch senses.

topics.headline: request points to the attribute answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final attribute as the answer to the root-quality being sought.
topics.reason: The same root appears locally in the requestive verb and then in the intensive predicate, with a clear role shift from seeking to possessing.

topics.headline: Surah 5 covering-mercy pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader links this request to Surah 5's recurring covering-and-mercy closures, including 5:3, 5:34, 5:39, and 5:98.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide concrete same-surah references and the local final predicate confirms the formulaic field.

topics.headline: wrong covering answered by sought covering
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the warning's exposure and wrong-covering field reverse into a request for protective divine covering.
topics.reason: The boundary and sound rows are locally coherent because the ayah moves from 5:73's threat into a request whose root recurs in the answer.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction launching a new nominal answer clause after the coordinated question
words.prose: The second {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is not the same kind of connector as the first. It resumes the discourse and starts a fresh nominal sentence, so the ayah pivots from the human actions not being done to what God already is. Its attached surface lets the answer begin at once, but the clause boundary keeps that answer from becoming another coordinated verb.

topics.headline: new declarative answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammar shift from question to declarative answer.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify word 8 as resumptive, opening an independent nominal clause rather than coordinating with the verbs.

topics.headline: from missing action to divine attribute
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the discourse turn from what they fail to do to the divine reality that makes return possible.
topics.reason: The clause boundary after the requestive verb and before the divine-name subject supports the pivot described by the CRITICAL rows.

topics.headline: attached but boundary-making
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the answer begin immediately while still crossing a clause boundary.
topics.reason: The particle attaches to the new divine-name subject while the grammar marks a new nominal sentence.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name in nominative subject position, launching the stable attribute answer
words.root_gloss_range: {{ar:أ ل ه}} ({{tr:ʾ-l-h}}) includes worship and disputed bewilderment derivations; locally the fixed proper name is the subject of the closing predicates
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:allāhu}}) restates the divine name instead of letting the prior suffix carry the reference. The nominative form makes God the subject of a nominal attribute statement, shifting the same name from endpoint and requested object to explicit possessor of covering and mercy. That repetition gathers the return, covering, and mercy fields into a formulaic answer and bookends the ayah's movement: toward God, then God as the source of the answer. After the human claim in 5:73, discourse control returns to God named as subject of mercy.

topics.headline: name restated as subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer deliberately names God again rather than relying on a pronoun.
topics.reason: QAC marks this occurrence as nominative subject of the nominal sentence, distinct from the earlier genitive goal and suffix reference.

topics.headline: stable bearer of the predicates
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees forgiveness and mercy presented as stable divine attributes, not isolated events.
topics.reason: The two following predicates attach to this subject in a nominal clause, supporting the stable-attribute payoff.

topics.headline: goal becomes answer subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same name from return-destination to source of the requested qualities.
topics.reason: The local repetition is functional: word 5 is the goal of turning and word 9 is the subject of the closing attributes.

topics.headline: divine-name field centered in the formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the divine name gather the return, covering, and mercy fields while the fixed proper name remains the selected local form.
topics.reason: Derivational and formulaic pressures are useful, but they are narrowed by the local nominative proper-name subject.

topics.headline: from claimed object to subject of mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the discourse move from human claims about God to God named as subject of the answer.
topics.reason: The boundary rows fit the local clause shift: the final nominal sentence begins with God as explicit subject after the polemical question.

words.gloss_range: indefinite intensive predicate naming God's abundant, stable covering/forgiving quality
words.root_gloss_range: {{ar:غ ف ر}} ({{tr:gh-f-r}}) includes covering, concealment, and forgiveness; local faʿūl predicate selects intensive divine forgiveness/protective covering

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: second predicate paired with the covering attribute

words.prose: {{ar:غَفُورٌۭ}} ({{tr:ghafūrun}}) answers the requestive verb by turning the sought {{ar:غ ف ر}} ({{tr:gh-f-r}}) quality into God's predicate. Its faʿūl shape makes covering and forgiveness stable and abundant, not a single event, and the indefinite predicate form pairs it with {{ar:رَّحِيمٌ}} ({{tr:raḥīmun}}) as a coupled closure. The root's covering image remains narrowed to divine forgiveness and protection, and its first position in the pair lets covering address exposed fault before mercy completes restoration. As a repeated Surah 5 closing, the attribute is available across different faults rather than belonging only to one offense.

topics.headline: abundant stable covering
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees forgiveness presented as an enduring divine attribute rather than a one-time act.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an intensive predicate of the nominal sentence, supporting the CRITICAL faʿūl and stable-attribute claims.

topics.headline: covering image as forgiveness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels forgiveness as protective covering while the local predicate keeps the meaning within divine pardon.
topics.reason: V4 supports covering and forgiveness, but local divine predicate grammar narrows broad physical branches into the forgiveness/protection attribute.

topics.headline: sought root becomes possessed quality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final predicate as the direct answer to what the previous verb asks for.
topics.reason: The same root appears in the requestive verb at word 7 and the intensive predicate at word 10, with role shift from seeking to possessing.

topics.headline: paired indefinite closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the two final qualities as a coupled formula rather than isolated adjectives.
topics.reason: The final two words share predicate shape and recognized formulaic pairing, while the local question specializes the formula as an answer.

topics.headline: covering before mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the closure move from covering exposed fault to the mercy that follows.
topics.reason: The order of the two predicates and the boundary reversal rows are locally coherent: {{ar:غَفُورٌ}} ({{tr:ghafūrun}}) precedes {{ar:رَّحِيمٌ}} ({{tr:raḥīmun}}).

topics.headline: formula available across faults
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the covering attribute as a reusable divine closure, not a crime-specific exception.
topics.reason: Contextual evidence supports frequent divine-attribute deployment, and the local ayah specializes it through the preceding request.

words.gloss_range: second intensive predicate naming enduring divine mercy and completing the paired closure
words.root_gloss_range: {{ar:ر ح م}} ({{tr:r-ḥ-m}}) ranges across mercy, tenderness, kinship, and womb imagery; local faʿīl predicate selects enduring divine mercy with nurturing pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: first predicate in the closing covering-mercy pair

words.prose: {{ar:رَّحِيمٌۭ}} ({{tr:raḥīmun}}) completes the answer by landing the ayah on mercy. It matches {{ar:غَفُورٌ}} ({{tr:ghafūrun}}) in predicate shape and tanwīn cadence, while its faʿīl pattern presents mercy as enduring quality. The womb-and-tenderness field is narrowed to the divine mercy attribute, adding nurturing restoration after covering; this tawba-to-mercy structure also recalls 2:37 while 5:74 keeps its own covering-mercy pair. As the final word, it turns the rebuking question and the painful-warning field of 5:73 into an appeal whose last sound and meaning are mercy.

topics.headline: matched second predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees mercy bound into the same nominal closure as covering, not added as an unrelated clause.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:رَّحِيمٌ}} ({{tr:raḥīmun}}) as the second predicate and attachment evidence links it with the same divine-name subject.

topics.headline: mercy as enduring quality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears mercy as a stable divine quality rather than a temporary reaction.
topics.reason: The intensive adjectival pattern and nominal predication support durable attribute force.

topics.headline: nurturing mercy image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels mercy as nurturing tenderness while local grammar keeps the selected sense as divine mercifulness.
topics.reason: V4 supports mercy, kinship, and womb imagery, but the local faʿīl predicate selects the divine mercy attribute rather than concrete womb terms.

topics.headline: covering then nurturing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final pair unfold from covering fault to nurturing restoration.
topics.reason: The local order places {{ar:رَّحِيمٌ}} ({{tr:raḥīmun}}) after {{ar:غَفُورٌ}} ({{tr:ghafūrun}}), supporting the staged-pair payoff.

topics.headline: ayah lands on mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that after warning and rebuke, the final semantic and acoustic landing is mercy.
topics.reason: The word is final in the ayah and closes the nominal answer after the rebuking question.

topics.headline: mercy formula specializes the invitation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader links the tawba-to-mercy structure here with the tawba-response pattern in 2:37 while keeping 5:74's own covering-mercy pair.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete references and formula evidence; local syntax specializes the formula as the answer to this question.

topics.headline: audible sealed pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the two predicates close as one balanced audible unit.
topics.reason: The matching final tanwīn and long-vowel predicate cadence support the CRITICAL sound rows.

topics.headline: threat handed off to mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the painful-warning field of 5:73 handed off to a mercy-response possibility in 5:74.
topics.reason: The boundary rows are coherent with the final word's local position and with the same-surah mercy-response closure pattern.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired constructions يَتُوبُونَ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ and يَسْتَغْفِرُونَهُ direct both the turn and the request toward God.
baseline_models.mechanism: The interrogative solicits a response, the preposition gives that response a destination, and the attached object pronoun makes the same destination the addressee of the request. Repentance is therefore a relational movement completed as petition, not an undirected change of mood.

activation_trace.role: The solicited-turn branch makes the rhetorical question an offered opening that calls for an answering return.
The worship branch identifies the destination and repeated divine subject as the one to whom allegiance and petition are redirected.
The moral-covering branch turns the second verb into an explicit request that the returned relationship deal with the fault and its effect.

changed_reading.before: Repentance is simply feeling regret and asking for pardon.
changed_reading.after: Repentance is an answering movement toward God that becomes concrete by addressing the same God for protection from the fault's effect.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The root غ ف ر occurs first as their requested action and then as God's standing predicate, followed by رَّحِيمٌ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The requested covering is answered by a predicate of abundant covering capacity. Its material branch adds preservation as well as concealment, while the mercy predicate prevents that cover from reading as mere suppression: it is tender protection of the exposed wrongdoer.

activation_trace.role: The physical-cover branch contributes a layer that both hides and preserves, giving forgiveness a protective material logic.
The fault-covering branch specifies that the protection concerns sin and the damaging consequence that follows it.
Tender mercy supplies the affective force by which the protective covering serves the person rather than merely hiding evidence.

changed_reading.before: Forgiveness is a legal cancellation appended to repentance.
changed_reading.after: The returning person asks to be covered and preserved from an exposed fault by a divine disposition explicitly characterized as tender mercy.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The packet maps يَتُوبُونَ not only to ت و ب but also to the split target ت ب ب.
baseline_models.mechanism: The split inventory places loss and destruction beside the restoration of a prepared, straight, continuing course. Carried cautiously, the focus turn can be modeled as a reversal from a trajectory that wastes itself into one that becomes viable and steady.

activation_trace.role: The loss branch supplies the terminal trajectory from which the invited turn withdraws.
The restored-course branch supplies the contrasting outcome of steadiness, readiness, and continuity after the turn.

changed_reading.before: Turning describes only a change of direction.
changed_reading.after: The turn may also mark a change of viability: departure from a self-consuming course into one that can stand, continue, and become clear.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context supplies opposed uses of covering. One cover blocks truth; another removes bad deeds by covering them. The focus request for غفر then reverses both agent and object: the person relinquishes concealment of truth and seeks God's protective concealment of an acknowledged fault.

activation_trace.role: Protective covering at the focus becomes the destination of a reversal in how covering is used.
Expiatory covering supplies the nearby positive model in which bad deeds, rather than truth, are what get covered over.
Truth-blocking covering supplies the failed defensive posture that the focus invitation asks the hearers to reverse.

structural_cues: 5:65 promises expiatory covering, 5:73 indicts truth-concealment, and 5:74 immediately offers a request for a different covering.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies three cover-images; I infer a reversal from self-protective concealment to disclosed fault under divine protection. A live alternative is that the roots merely carry independent conventional senses without a designed material reversal.

changed_reading.before: Seeking forgiveness means asking for a fault to be hidden.
changed_reading.after: Seeking forgiveness means stopping the concealment of truth so that an admitted fault, rather than truth itself, can receive protective covering.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding ayah sets a threshold: cease the saying, or painful consequence will make contact. The focus invitation occupies the interval between cessation and contact, so return plus protective covering reads as an available interception before the threatened effect lands.

activation_trace.role: The preserving cover supplies the barrier sought at the open threshold before harmful contact.
Cessation and restraint define the first side of the threshold that repentance must cross.
The arrival of an effect by contact defines the threatened second side that protective forgiveness can intercept.

structural_cues: The unfulfilled condition in 5:73 is followed directly by the interrogative invitation in 5:74 before the discourse resumes its argument.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies cessation, threatened contact, and a covering request; I infer a temporal arrow in which the request can interrupt contact. Alternatively, 5:73 may state consequence and 5:74 mercy without inviting a material shield sequence.

changed_reading.before: Forgiveness repairs damage after punishment has become due.
changed_reading.after: The ayah opens a last interval in which cessation, return, and requested covering can prevent the threatened consequence from making contact.

context_deltas.mechanism: The command to worship God and the later test of powerless objects specify what turning إِلَى ٱللَّهِ changes. The penitent redirects submission and need toward the only addressee presented as able to dispose of outcomes, hear the petition, and know its condition.

activation_trace.role: The worship branch makes the named destination of return a redirection of allegiance, not merely a location.
Submissive worship supplies the positive orientation to God that the focus return resumes.
The same worship image, now questioned when directed elsewhere, identifies the practical misdirection being reversed.
Effective possession and disposal distinguish a capable object of dependence from one unable to alter harm or benefit.
Divine hearing makes the focus request an addressed and receivable petition rather than a ritual utterance into incapacity.
Uncovered knowledge supplies the addressee's access to the condition for which covering is requested.

structural_cues: 5:72 commands worship of God, 5:75 emphasizes creaturely dependence on food, and 5:76 contrasts powerless worship objects with God's hearing and knowledge.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies worship, incapacity, hearing, and knowledge; I infer that repentance redirects dependency and petition to the uniquely responsive agent. A live alternative is that the focus calls for ethical retraction without making worship-address the governing mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Turning to God is a generic moral reorientation.
changed_reading.after: Turning to God withdraws worship and dependency from incapable objects and readdresses both allegiance and the plea for cover to the one who can hear, know, and act.

context_deltas.mechanism: Before the focus, blindness and deafness recur even after a divine turning. After it, another response runs in the opposite order: hearing becomes recognition, recognition overfills the eyes with tears, and the overflow becomes declared belief. This stages repentance as recovered permeability to evidence, embodied and spoken rather than merely inward.

activation_trace.role: The solicited turn at the focus becomes the open question to which the later receptive sequence can function as an enacted answer.
Loss of inward sight supplies one closed channel whose recurrence shows that an earlier reopening did not become durable.
Failure to listen supplies the paired closure that the later act of hearing reverses.
Hearing as understanding and response initiates the successful receptive sequence.
Easy abundant flow gives the inward recognition an involuntary outward passage through the eyes.
The tear and its channel make changed perception bodily visible rather than leaving it as an untestable claim.
Recognition by a discernible mark supplies the cognitive hinge between receiving the message and confessing belief.

structural_cues: 5:71 has closure, divine turning, then repeated closure; 5:83 has hearing, recognition, tears, and confession; 5:84-85 continue into hope and accepted reward.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mirrored closed and open sensory sequences; I infer that the later sequence performs the kind of return asked for in 5:74. The materially live alternative is that 5:71 and 5:83 concern different groups and are contrastive examples, not stages of one conversion process.

changed_reading.before: Repentance is an invisible decision reported by the speaker.
changed_reading.after: The requested turn can be recognized as reopened hearing and discernment whose pressure becomes tears, confession, and a new communal trajectory.

context_deltas.mechanism: The pericope places a bad recompense at 5:60 and a good recompense at 5:85. Between them, the focus split target contrasts destruction with a course made stable. The invited turn can therefore function as the hinge that changes what comes back to the actor.

activation_trace.role: The destruction branch supplies the adverse endpoint associated with refusing the turn.
The stable-course branch supplies the viable endpoint made available by the turn.
Recompense as an action returning to its actor supplies the adverse framing pole before the focus.
The same returning-recompense image supplies the favorable pole after receptive confession.

structural_cues: 5:60 names a worse recompense, while 5:83-85 move from reception and confession to divine reward, bracketing 5:74 with opposed returned outcomes.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a split focus mapping and two recompense recurrences; I infer that repentance reroutes the outcome returning to the actor. The alternative is a loose rhetorical bracket, since ت و ب, its ت ب ب split, and ث و ب are form-distant and not one lexical branch.

changed_reading.before: Repentance changes only the actor's present stance.
changed_reading.after: Repentance becomes a hinge that reroutes the returning consequence, away from loss and toward a stable course whose action can return as favorable recompense.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the medical relapse branch of غ ف ر rather than its ordinary moral branch. It remains anchored in the focus's repeated غ ف ر and in 5:71's explicit improvement-then-renewed-closure sequence. Downstream prose should present it only as an exploratory relapse analogy, never as the lexical meaning of forgiveness or as a diagnosis.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The request يَسْتَغْفِرُونَهُ and predicate غَفُورٌ repeat غ ف ر around a context that has already shown reopening followed by relapse.

activation_trace.role: The wound-or-illness relapse branch makes forgiveness imaginable as protection against deterioration after an apparent recovery.
Repeated inward blindness supplies the relapse pattern after the intervening divine turn.
Repeated failure to listen confirms that the recovered condition can close again rather than remaining healed.

changed_reading.before: Forgiveness remits a completed past fault.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the plea also asks that a reopened moral-perceptual wound be kept from relapsing after the turn.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it carries the womb branch of ر ح م into a spatial sequence of refuge, entry, and covered garden. It remains anchored in رَّحِيمٌ and the focus's protective غ ف ر, while the context supplies opposed enclosures. Render it as a cross-domain image of re-housing under mercy, not as a claim that رَّحِيمٌ literally denotes a womb here.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The protective cover of غ ف ر is immediately qualified by رَّحِيمٌ, whose inventory includes a life-bearing enclosure.

activation_trace.role: The life-bearing enclosure supplies a contained image for mercy as a place of protected re-formation.
The preserving cover joins mercy to the spatial logic of being sheltered rather than left exposed.
Joining a gathering refuge supplies the adverse enclosure from which the focus invitation offers a change of destination.
Entry supplies the actual transition into a different containing community after recognition and belief.
The tree-covered garden supplies the favorable enclosure in which the redirected person is finally housed.

changed_reading.before: Mercy is a divine affect appended to the promise of forgiveness.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, mercy re-houses the returned person: from a destructive refuge into preserving cover, communal entry, and a life-bearing enclosure.

strongest_changes: Seeking forgiveness became a reversal of covering: stop hiding truth and receive protective cover over acknowledged fault.
The adjacency of cessation and threatened contact made 5:74 an interval for interception before consequence lands.
Turning to God became redirected worship and dependency toward the only capable, hearing, knowing addressee.
The later hearing-recognition-tears sequence supplied an embodied answer to the earlier relapse into blindness and deafness.
summary.what_was_special: The split ت و ب to ت ب ب mapping, together with opposed ث و ب recompenses, exposed a return-of-outcome hinge; the less expected relapse and womb branches of غ ف ر and ر ح م also supported contained medical and shelter analogies.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether 5:83-85 is intended as the enacted answer to 5:74 or as a contrast involving a separate subgroup.
How much weight the form-distant relation among ت و ب, the mapped ت ب ب target, and ث و ب can bear.
Whether the material-cover and re-enclosing-shelter models clarify the sequence or overextend branch analogies.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The threatened contact remains interruptible by protective covering.** `غ ف ر B001` is covering and `B002` shielding from consequence, joined to `ر ح م B001` tenderness. After 5:73's painful touch, I infer that return and seeking forgiveness insert a shield between formulation and consequence; warning remains an opening, not closure.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The threat remains adjacent to a route into shielding.** Fixed **غ ف ر / B001** (“protective covering”) and **B002** (“forgiving and shielding from consequence”) are requested and then restated as divine qualities. The prior two ayat announce barring and painful contact; the next ayat expose creaturely dependence and warn against excess. I infer from this immediate placement that correction is intended to move the addressees under protection before the threatened consequence closes upon them. The question reads as an open causal exit, not a tonal interruption of condemnation.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:75–5:76 showed what the open route asks them to acknowledge: creaturely dependence and lack of independent disposal, before 5:77 warns against desire-driven excess.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın eylem çekirdeğini türemiş eylem ve varlık adlarından ayırır; türemiş biçimlerin kapsamı yalın eylemin tamamına aktarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir varlığa tapınma eylemini ve kişinin kendini tapınmaya vermesini anlatır. Türemiş kullanımlarda bir varlığı tapınılır kılmayı, tapınılan varlığı ve tapınma konusu sayılan varlıkları da adlandırır.

facets.statement: Temel eylem, bir varlığa tapınmak ve kişinin kendini bu tapınmaya vermesidir.
Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
Ettirgen kullanım, bir varlığı başkalarınca tapınılır duruma getirme veya öyle sunma işlemini bildirir.
Güneşe kimi topluluklarca tapınılması nedeniyle ona tapınılan varlık anlamındaki bir ad verilmesi, varlık anlamının tarihsel bir örneğidir.

facets.statement: Bir başkasının durumu karşısında yüreğin yumuşaması, ona acıma ve içten yakınlık duyma çekirdeği oluşturur.

Bir kimsenin Tanrı'nın esirgemesine erişmesini dilemek, çekirdek anlamdan doğan kalıplaşmış bir söz eylemidir.
Tanrı hakkında kullanıldığında esirgemenin genişliği ve yaratılmışlara iyilik olarak ulaşması belirginleşir.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu, işte yumuşak davranma, geçimli olma, iyi davranış, koruma ve uygunlaştırma gibi daha geniş alanlara uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da sertlikten uzak davranma, başkasını gözetme ve ona iyilik ulaştırma alanında kesişir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın çıkış noktası başkasına acıyan iç yöneliştir; komşu ise acıma bulunmadan da yumuşak yöntem ve iyi davranış bildirebilir. Dolayısıyla ortak sonuçlar üretseler de çekirdekleri farklıdır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dalda iyilik, başkasına acıma ve yürek yumuşaklığının gerektirdiği bir sonuçtur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, yapılan işin iyi ve düzgün olmasını ya da adaletin ötesinde yarar sağlamayı, acıma şartı olmadan kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: acımanın doğurduğu iyilik ile iyi eylem
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal başkasına yarar ulaştırma ve iyi davranma sonucunda buluşabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: İyi eylem çok çeşitli nedenlerle ve hatta bir nesneyi düzgün yapma biçiminde gerçekleşebilir. Odak anlam ise kişiye yönelen acıma ve esirgeme temeline bağlıdır; bu yüzden sonuç ortaklığı çekirdek eşitliği oluşturmaz.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Sunulan bütün adaylar değerlendirildi. En yakın üç duygu dalı ile yumuşak davranış ve iyi eylem dalları sınırı gerçekten aydınlattığı için seçildi; cimrilik, iyilik yapma coşkusu, eşlik ederek koruma ve aynı kökün öteki üç dalı ya yalnızca uzak bir karşıtlık ya da ayrı bir anlam alanı sunduğundan yayımlanmadı.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak anlatımı, dişi bedenindeki bu organı yavrunun başladığı, karın içinde taşındığı ve geliştiği yer ve kap olarak tanımlar. Hazırlanan dal çerçevesi organı soy ilişkisinden, acıma anlamından ve organın hastalık durumundan doğru biçimde ayırır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal bağımsız organ adını ve onun çoğulunu kapsar; herhangi bir kalıba bağlı yan anlam bu yalın tanıma eklenmez.

concept_map.definition: Dişinin karnında yavrunun tutunup geliştiği, onu doğuma kadar içinde taşıyan iç organdır.

facets.statement: Dişi bedenindeki bu iç organ, yavrunun oluşup geliştiği yer ve onu karın içinde taşıyan kap işlevindedir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlatım, dişi ya da kadın bedenindeki organı yavrunun başladığı yer ve karın içindeki taşıyıcı kap olarak tanımlar. Tekil biçim organı, çoğul biçim ise aynı tür organları adlandırır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Dişi bedeninde yavrunun tutunup geliştiği belirli iç organı doğal ve kısa bir Türkçe karşılıkla anlatır.

error_profile.preserves: Organın yavrunun gelişme ve taşınma yeri oluşunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Teknik organ adının bilinmediği veya organın işlevinin açıkça belirtilmesi gereken bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Bedensel organ niteliğini ve yavrunun gelişme yeri olma işlevini korur.
Türkçedeki yerleşik kullanımında aynı bedensel organı doğru olarak gösterebilir.
error_profile.collision: Kaynak dildeki organ adını doğrudan yinelediği ve aynı ses dizisi başka adlandırmalarda da bulunduğu için açıklayıcı karşılık görevini yerine getirmez.

error_profile.preserves: Organın bulunduğu genel beden bölgesini korur.
error_profile.adds: Döl yatağı dışındaki bütün karın boşluğunu ve başka organları kapsama ekler.
error_profile.collision: Belirli iç organı onun bulunduğu daha geniş beden bölgesiyle karıştırır.

error_profile.preserves: Yavrunun anne bedeninde taşındığı yer düşüncesini korur.
error_profile.adds: Belirli organın dışındaki bütün karın bölgesini ve yalnızca gebelik durumunu kapsama ekler.
error_profile.collision: Organın kendisiyle annenin genel karın bölgesini birbirine karıştırır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, dişi bedeninde yavrunun geliştiği somut iç organı adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, ortak soydan gelen kişiler arasındaki toplumsal ilişkiyi ve yakınlığı adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Soy ilişkisi, aynı doğum kaynağından çıkma düşüncesiyle organ adından geliştirilmiştir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak bedensel bir organdır; komşu ise o organın ortak köken imgesi üzerinden adlandırılan kişiler arası bağdır. Tarihsel kavram bağlantısı, somut organ ile soyut ilişkiyi eş anlamlı yapmaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak, yavruyu içinde taşıyan anneye ait organın kendisidir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu, henüz doğmamış ve anne karnında gizli bulunan yavrunun kendisidir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal doğumdan önce anne bedenindeki gelişme sürecinin aynı yer ve katılımcılarını konu edinir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak yavrunun bulunduğu ve geliştiği organdır, komşu ise bu organın içinde gelişen canlıdır. Taşıyan yapı ile taşınan yavru aynı bağlamda görünse de birbirinin yerine kullanılamaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak, gebelik olsun ya da olmasın bedende bulunan organı adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu, döllenmiş yavrunun bu organda yerleşmesi olayını ve yerleşmiş gebelik durumunu anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal, yavrunun döl yatağında yerleşip gelişmeye başlaması bağlamında doğrudan buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak kalıcı beden yapısıdır; komşu o yapının içinde gerçekleşen belirli bir başlangıç olayıdır. Organın varlığı gebeliğin yerleşmiş olmasını gerektirmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak, yavrunun gelişme yeri olan iç organın anatomik kimliğini bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu, belirli zamanda bu organdan gelen kanı, kanama olayını, zamanı ve ilgili durumu bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal dişi üreme bedenini ve aynı organla bağlantılı olayları konu edinir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak bir organın adıdır; komşu ise o organla ilişkili kan ve dönemsel bedensel olaydır. Aynı anatomik alanı paylaşmaları çekirdeklerini birleştirmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak, dişinin yavruyu taşıyan organının bütününü adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu, özellikle dişi devenin bu organındaki damarları ya da dar bir bölgeyi adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal aynı organın anatomik alanında ve özellikle dişi hayvan bedeninde buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak bütün organdır; komşu ise o organ içinde bulunan belirli damar veya bölgedir. Bütün ile onun küçük anatomik parçası birbirinin yerine geçmez.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi. Soy bağıyla ad aktarımı, organın içindeki yavru, gebeliğin yerleşmesi, dönemsel kanama ve organdaki damarlar en açıklayıcı sınırları verdi; gebelik ürünleri, karın içi, şişmanlık ve aynı kökün acıma ile hastalık dalları ya seçilen ayrımları yineledi ya da yalnızca uzak bir beden bağlamı sundu.
